newsitem.title: MEXICO: Three dead in new scandal at Mexican food agency.
newsitem.headline: Three dead in new scandal at Mexican food agency.

text.p: Three members of a family were murdered in connection with a new fraud scandal at Mexico's troubled government food agency Conasupo, its head said on Monday.

Conasupo Director General Humberto Mosconi told Televisa's nightly 24-Horas television news broadcast that the three dead -- a man, his wife and their son -- were among the main beneficiaries of some 20 million pesos ($3 million) syphoned off from the agency in late 1995 and early 1996.
"These people had previously been accused by Conasupo because they were the main shareholders of one of the companies that benefited from the money," he said.
He did not make clear when they were murdered.

The scandal followed allegations of massive irregularities at Conasupo, the government's main food distribution agency while under the stewardship from 1988-1992 of Raul Salinas, brother of then-President Carlos Salinas.
Newspapers recently reported that Mexican and U.S. investigators were probing allegations of money-laundering at Conasupo during Raul Salinas' tenure.
But the latest scandal was unconnected with Raul, Mosconi said, and occurred almost a year after his brother left the presidency in December 1994.

So far one person has been arrested in connection with the latest fraud, and arrest warrants have been issued for seven others, Televisa said. Raul Salinas was jailed in 1995 on murder charges apparently unconnected with Conasupo, and embezzlement charges. He has denied them.
